title: delta* count = n*K: the budget q*eps* ~ n is exactly ONE mu_n-orbit; F1=F3=F10=F9 collapse
evidence: Exact integer probe over mu_n proper subgroups at prize-regime primes (dyadic n=8,16,32; q=1 mod n, q~n^4, n<<sqrt q; q in {4129,4153} for n=8, {65537,65617} for n=16, 1048609 for n=32). I compute the bad-scalar set directly from the in-tree Vieta/far-line description lacBad(mu_n,a,t)={e_t(S): S subset mu_n, |S|=a, e_1(S)=...=e_{t-1}(S)=0}, t=a-b, the worst monomial direction (a,b)=(k+t,k), and decompose it into <g^t>-orbits. TWO falsifications. (A) The headline identity '#bad = n*K + eps, exactly ONE mu_n-orbit of size n' is FALSE for general directions: the multiplier is c=g^(b-a) of order ord(c)=n/gcd(t,n), so the quantum is n/gcd(t,n), NOT n, whenever gcd(t,n)>1. Clean field-independent counterexample at n=8, t=2 (a=4, delta=1/2): #bad=5 = 4*1+1 = (n/gcd(2,8))*K+eps with quantum 4 (NOT 8) and K=1 -- 5 is NOT of the form 8*K+eps for any integer K. Same at both primes q=4129 and q=4153, confirming it is structural. (Both n=8 t=4 gives quantum 2, n=16 t=2 gives quantum 8, t=4 quantum 4, etc.) The in-tree lemma C004 cites (adjacent_card_eq_n_mul_add_zero) is correctly stated ONLY for the adjacent pair t=1 (multiplier g, order n); C004 over-generalizes it to all forms. (B) The NOVEL threshold claim 'delta* is EXACTLY where K crosses from O(1) to >=2' and 'budget I(delta)<=n reads K<=1+o(1)' is REFUTED decisively: for the adjacent (t=1, KKH26 extremal) direction at its cleanest radius delta=1-(k+1)/n, the orbit count K=#bad/n does NOT sit near 1 -- it GROWS like q/n. Measured K (=#bad/n) at the adjacent direction: n=8 -> K=5 (#bad=40); n=16 -> K=141 (rho=1/4, #bad=2256) and K=205 (rho=1/2, #bad=3280); n=32 -> K=32745 (rho=1/4, #bad=1047840) and K=32769 (rho=1/2, #bad~q). At n=32 the bad set is essentially ALL of F_q (#bad ~ q), so K ~ q/n, not 1. K jumps 0 -> hundreds/thousands with NO 'crosses 1->2' plateau; the budget #bad<=q*eps*~n (K<=1) is violated by factor K~141..32745, i.e. exactly the I(delta)=Theta(growing) Gauss-period incidence, not '1+o(1)'. Probes: scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C004_orbit_threshold.py, probe_C004_Kgrowth.py (n=8/16 brute), probe_C004_n32.py (size-constrained subset-sum DP).
reduced_to: The genuinely PROVEN content (in-tree, axiom-clean) survives and is correctly scoped: for the ADJACENT monomial pair (X^a, X^{a+1}) on a smooth domain of order n, #bad = n*q + [0 in badSet] -- n | #(badSet minus {0}) exactly (n_dvd_card_badScalars_adjacent / adjacent_card_eq_n_mul_add_zero); for general (a,b) the quantum is the orbit order n/gcd(t,n) (orderOf_dvd_card_badScalars_erase_zero). This is an exact divisibility/quantization law, NOT a threshold pin. The sharp open quantity it correctly localizes is the integer K(delta) = #(badSet minus 0)/(n/gcd(t,n)) = the number of free <g^t>-orbits = the number of distinct subleading-coefficient values e_t(S) modulo the dilation action -- and the prize is to show this orbit count is bounded (K = O(1), giving #bad = O(n)) in the window interior, NOT that K crosses 1. Bounding the orbit count K IS the BGK/Gauss-period sup-norm problem in disguise (K ~ q/n at the cleanest radius means full spreading; pulling K down to O(1) in the window is the sqrt-cancellation among (q-1)/n Gauss-period phases).
wall: BGK / generalized-Paley (Gauss-period) sup-norm wall. The orbit count K(delta) = #(distinct dilation-classes of subset sums e_t(S)) grows like q/n at the extremal adjacent radius; forcing K=O(1) in the window interior is equivalent to the incomplete character-sum / Paley-graph-eigenvalue bound for thin mu_n (the 25-year-open core, face 3 of CLAUDE.md). The orbit-counting reframing does NOT move off this wall -- it restates the same growing incidence I(delta)=Theta(.) as 'K is large', which is exactly the deep-moment/Gauss-period count already quantified (memory arklib-389-deep-moment-wall: B ~ sqrt(n log) not sqrt n).
honest_note: I did NOT refute the in-tree Lean lemmas -- they are genuine and axiom-clean; what is refuted is C004's INTERPRETATION layer: (i) the 'n*K, exactly one orbit of size n' collapse is only valid for adjacent/t-coprime-to-n directions, and FAILS for dyadic even-t directions where the orbit shrinks to n/gcd(t,n) (exact counterexample #bad=5 at n=8 t=2, both primes); (ii) the central novel claim that delta* is the K:1->2 crossing and the budget reads K<=1 is false -- K is hundreds-to-tens-of-thousands at the extremal radius and grows like q/n, so 'the budget n is literally one orbit' does not hold and there is no 1->2 crossing at delta*. The forms-collapse F1=F3=F9=F10 onto a single counting identity is real and useful as a reframing, but the identity it collapses to is '#bad = (n/gcd(t,n))*K + eps with K a growing orbit count', which RE-DERIVES the BGK wall rather than pinning delta*. This echoes the already-logged S3/N1 refutation (DISPROOF_LOG: the naive orbit-count/flat-numerator law is off by the projective infinity-slot and the maximizer is one PROJECTIVE orbit) -- C004 is the dyadic-direction analogue: the orbit size and count both move with (t,n) and delta, so a single 'one orbit = n' reading is not a theorem. Probes are exact (no sampling) at multiple proper-subgroup large primes; n=32 used a size-constrained subset-sum reachability DP (exact). Worth appending the even-t quantum counterexample and the K-growth table to DISPROOF_LOG.
